newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar subsides after overnight surge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar subsides after overnight surge.

text.p: The Singapore dollar gave up some ground to corporate buying interest in the U.S. dollar on Thursday, but dealers said the market would be wary of pushing it down again after its sudden rise on Wednesday.

The U.S. dollar's sudden drop against the majors on news of an unexpectedly large U.S. trade deficit for July caused the staid Singapore unit to gain about 40 points as stop-loss U.S. dollar sales were triggered in a thin market, dealers said.

"The market was caught long yesterday. There'd been a lot of buying (of dollar/Sing) so when the dollar/yen and dollar/mark fell, it triggered stop-loss sales below the 1.41 level," said a European bank dealer.
But he said the U.S. dollar looked well supported at around S$1.4065/70 on corporate buying interest.
"Some people are buying dollar/Sing at around 1.4065/70 because that's the level the MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) is thought to have intervened," said another dealer.
The MAS, Singapore's de facto central bank, tends to intervene whenever the Singapore dollar shows signs of appreciating too sharply against its U.S. counterpart.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4065/70 to the U.S. dollar in late afternoon trade against an opening 1.4055/65.
Andy Tan, economist and general manager at MMS International, said the U.S. dollar would have difficulty appreciating back towards S$1.41.
"It caught a lot of traders by surprise, so I don't think people are in a hurry to push it back. If it does go above 1.41, I think there'll be a lot of selling interest," Tan said.
